title: A sour mango tastes good to hunger
literal_meaning: To a hungry mouth, a sour mango is tasty.
meaning_odia: ଭୋକିଲା ପାଟିକୁ ଆମ୍ବିଳା ଆମ୍ବ ବି ସୁଆଦ ଲାଗେ—ପଙ୍କ୍ତି ଭୋକ ଓ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ରୁଚିକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ିଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ଦରକାର ତୀବ୍ର ହେଲେ ସାଧାରଣତଃ କମ୍ ପସନ୍ଦ ହୋଇପାରୁଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆଦର ପାଇପାରେ। ଏଠାରେ ଆମ୍ବିଳାର ଅର୍ଥ ପଚା ନୁହେଁ, ସୁଆଦର ଅର୍ଥ ମିଠା ହୋଇଯିବା ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: The mango remains sour, but the hungry mouth finds it pleasant. Read editorially, the saying shows how need can change appreciation. It describes a shift in the eater’s response, rather than a change in the fruit itself.
usage_example: Original imagined example: After a long morning without a meal, someone enjoys a simple snack they would usually pass over. A companion recalls the sour mango that tastes good to a hungry mouth.
cultural_context: The contrast is between ଆମ୍ବିଳା, sour, and ସୁଆଦ, pleasing to taste. They need not be opposites: the hungry mouth connects them. The wording gives no recipe, ripeness test or claim about food safety.

witnesses.locator: Page32, fifth and final item beginning ଭୋକିଲା ପାଟିକି.
